## Access & isolation (SAFE creds method — no plaintext)
SSH to .215 via the platform ssh2 approach (decrypt `server.rootPasswordEnc` for server id `cmsecmdps0001hlp27ai6mr7c`, pass straight into ssh2 password field, never echo it; mirror lib/sftp.ts). ASSERT hostname/IP 51.79.226.215 before commands. Isolated worktree off prod HEAD:
`git -C /opt/nexis worktree add /opt/nexis-wt-roles -b feature/roles origin/main` and build THERE with its own copied node_modules (Turbopack rejects symlinked node_modules). If classifier-blocked, report what's left.

## Understand first
The current auth: `src/lib/access.ts` (coarse `UserRole` enum — OWNER/ADMIN/INSTRUCTOR etc.), how the tenant `policies` are structured/persisted, how admin routes/pages currently gate access, the team-members area in Settings, and the Prisma User/membership model.

## Build — granular roles + permissions
- A **permission map**: define the discrete capabilities in the admin (e.g. manage_schedule, manage_clients, manage_billing, manage_settings, manage_team, view_analytics, run_pos, manage_website …) grounded in what the app actually has.
- **Role presets** (Owner = all; plus sensible presets like Manager, Front Desk, Instructor) stored as `policies.roles` (customizable per tenant) so a tenant can tune what each role can do, while keeping safe defaults when unset.
- A **`can(user, capability)` helper** and ENFORCE it across the admin server actions/route handlers and hide/disable UI a role can't use — not just cosmetic; the server must reject unauthorized actions. Keep the existing coarse enum working (map it onto the new capabilities) so nothing breaks for current users; Owner always retains full access.
- A **Team roles editor** in Settings: assign a role to each team member + edit what each role can do.

## Rules
- Prisma changes additive only (don't migrate the live DB — I'll `prisma db push`). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean + `npm run build` MUST pass in the worktree.
- Commit to `feature/roles`, push origin. Do NOT merge/deploy/restart.
- Board (Nxeon DB on /opt/nxeon): move card `cmsbkg0qd001rhlv5882s8t7y` to In progress (`cmsbk8miq0017hlv5elhzx9vf`) + "Claude" comment (what built, branch, deploy steps). Clean up helper scripts.

Report: the capability list, how presets + `can()` enforcement work, where it's enforced (server + UI), how legacy roles map, build/tsc status, and deploy steps.

The middleware will use default role presets without hitting the database, providing a coarse authorization gate, while the actual server-side code (pages and route handlers) enforces fine-grained tenant-specific policies by loading the full tenant configuration and calling the authorization check with the resolved capabilities. This way, if a tenant customizes a role, the middleware doesn't need to know about it—the authoritative check happens server-side.
